title.narrative: Emergency life-saving health response to distressed floods-affected and cholera-affected communities in Aweil East, Fangak, Nasir, Mayendit, and Rubkona counties in South Sudan

description.narrative: More than 710,00 people across 30 of the 78 counties in South Sudan and the Abyei Administrative Area have now been affected by floods. Heavy rains since May 2024, combined with the controlled release of water from Lake Victoria, have caused the Nile River to swell, exacerbating the flooding situation. The floods combined with a worsening humanitarian situation marked by severe food insecurity, economic decline, continued conflict, disease outbreaks, and the repercussions of the Sudan conflict have severely affected the country with Jonglei, Unity, and Warrap states reporting the highest numbers of affected population. Since May 2024, floods have caused extensive damage to homes, crops, and critical infrastructure, disrupting basic social services including health. As of 2nd of September, WHO had recorded 24 health facilities that have been flooded, 18 cases of snake bites, 2 cases of drowning, 2 deaths, and a surge in Malaria cases (94,511 cases across the country in week 34). As of the end of October 2024, a cholera outbreak has been declared in South Sudan, affecting more than 2,500 severe cases and 32 deaths across 18 counties in 6 states.WHO is requesting the Rapid Response allocation to initiate flood and cholera response and provide urgent life-saving health needs to 378,607 (155,228 women, 157,934 men, 30,830 boys, and 34615 girls) flood-affected and cholera-affected people across five priority counties of Aweil East, Fangak, Nasir, Mayendit, and Rubkona, and any other cholera-affected counties. The proposed project will ensure the delivery of life-saving primary health care services and cholera treatment while reducing the risk of further disease outbreaks, particularly vector-borne diseases which necessitate timely detection, investigation, and response.WHO will address the needs using three specific objectives that will (1) Ensure emergency primary healthcare for flood-affected populations (2) Strengthen disease surveillance and response systems during Floods, and (3) Ensure timely access to medical supplies and specific cholera response supplies in flood-affected high-risk areas. Specifically, WHO will engage both NGO partners and its emergency Mobile Medical Teams (eMMTs) to deliver emergency life-saving primary healthcare through static and mobile clinics, and cholera treatment through dedicated facilities, including ensuring the effectiveness of referral systems, and services tailored for vulnerable groups in hard-to-reach areas, and working with UNFPA to facilitate seamless service delivery that integrates Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) where UNFPA will provide human resources (nurses or midwives) and SRH supplies in areas where WHO or its implementing partners are offering health services and deliver SRH services. Where UNFPA is already partnering with IRC, WHO will supply medical countermeasures and any necessary technical support to ensure ongoing service provision. Implementing partners will also be dedicating resources to cholera-specific RCCE to improve community awareness and timely identification and referral of cholera cases. WHO will deploy Rapid Response Teams (RRTs) to ensure timely detection, investigation, and response to disease outbreaks while conducting regular water quality surveillance to mitigate the risks of water-borne diseases in flood and cholera affected locations. Finally, WHO will procure, transport, and distribute emergency medical supplies in flood-prone high-risk areas, and cholera treatment supplies to cholera-affected areas, to optimize the response capacities of emergency health actors. The proposed interventions will reduce preventable mortality and morbidity among the target population in line with the health cluster's strategic objectives of providing quality basic primary health care services and preventing health risks while strengthening the health care system as well as the 2024 South Sudan HRP's goals of saving lives, reducing health risks, and enhancing resilience.
